title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.3-5): Grothendieck wants an integral analogue of Sullivan's simplicial de Rham algebra. That is a functorial cochain algebra C^•_DR(X,Z) for a simplicial set X, obtained as Hom(X, DRS^•_*), where DRS^•_* is a simplicial (cosimplicial-in-n) commutative dga that resolves the coefficient ring.

Rationally (p.3) one takes DRS^•_[n] = Ω^•(Q[X_0..X_n]/(ΣX_i-1)) ≅ Q[X_0..X_{n-1}][dX_0..dX_{n-1}]. Two facts make it work: the algebraic Poincaré lemma, and the extendability (acyclicity) of each DRS^i_*. Over Z the Poincaré lemma fails because ∫x^n dx needs 1/(n+1). The cure is divided powers: the pd-polynomial de Rham complex Z<X_1..X_m>⊗Λ[dX] is a resolution of Z, since d(X^[k]) = X^[k-1]dX.

This page: the naive candidate is Z<X_0..X_n>[dX_i]/(ΣX_i-1, ΣdX_i)_pd. It does not make sense and is not ≅ Z<X_0..X_{n-1}>[dX_0..dX_{n-1}]. To eliminate X_n = 1-Σ_{i<n}X_i you need a pd-morphism Z<X_0..X_n> → Z<X_0..X_{n-1}> sending X_n to 1-ΣX_i. That element is not in the pd-ideal (augmentation ideal), so no such morphism exists. Equivalently, ΣX_i-1 is not in the pd-ideal, so one cannot form the pd-ideal it generates. Geometrically, the vertices (coordinate 1) of the standard simplex lie outside the pd-neighbourhood of the origin.

The fix is to work over a pd-base (S,J,γ) with a parameter t∈J and replace ΣX_i=1 by ΣX_i=t. This gives a 'simplex of size t' whose vertices t·e_i are pd-infinitesimally close to 0. Define
C^•_DRpd[n](S,J,t) = S<X_0..X_n>[dX_0..dX_n]/(ΣX_i-t, ΣdX_i)_pd.
This is legitimate because ΣX_i-t lies in the pd-ideal J·S<X>+S<X>^+ (p.5). Now X_n = t-Σ_{i<n}X_i is a pd-element, so the quotient is ≅ S<X_0..X_{n-1}>⊗Λ(dX_0..dX_{n-1}), a resolution of S.

As n varies, faces (X_i↦0) and degeneracies (X_i↦X_i+X_{i+1}) make this a cosimplicial pd-dga, augmented to S/J. For a simplicial scheme or simplicial set one then sets C^•_DRpd(X_*;S,J,t) = Hom(X_*, C^•_DRpd*(S,J,t)). Page 5 then notes that one only gets a map H_DRpd → H(X_*,S), not an isomorphism in general.

Aim: integral (or Z_p, e.g. S=Z_p, J=(p), t=p) commutative-cochain models for homotopy types. The universal case would be S=Z<t>, J=pd augmentation ideal. Over Q[t] with t inverted one recovers a rescaled Sullivan A_PL, so the construction is an integral pd-lattice in a degenerating family of Sullivan algebras.
errors: No mathematical error. The analysis of the 'hic' is correct: 1-ΣX_i is not in the pd-ideal, so the pd-quotient by ΣX_i-1 is undefined. The fix is sound: with t∈J, ΣX_i-t lies in the pd-ideal J S<X> + S<X>^+.

Gap (acknowledged on p.5): since the vertices t·e_i all reduce to the origin mod J, the resulting cochains need not compute H^*(X,S). Only a comparison map is claimed. The page does not check the second Sullivan condition (extendability/acyclicity of each C^i_DRpd* as a simplicial S-module), which over Z is the crux.

Minor: 'arbitraire de Z' should read 'over Z'. Also t must be in J for γ to apply. Over a Q-algebra J must be proper, so the Sullivan case t=1 is not literally a special case and is recovered only by inverting t.

ideas.what: Integral obstruction to Sullivan's polynomial forms (denominators in ∫x^n dx), cured by divided-power polynomial forms on simplices
ideas.modern_name: integral/divided-power models of Sullivan's A_PL; pd de Rham complex as integral resolution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational, 1977); integral attempts by Cenkl-Porter (early 1980s), Ekedahl (minimal models in integral homotopy theory, 2002); Mandell (E_∞ cochains, 2006) for the general integral problem
ideas.where_published: Only the unpublished 1976 IHES lecture notes (this cote); not in published Grothendieck texts as far as known

ideas.what: Replacing the standard simplex ΣX_i=1 by the pd-infinitesimal simplex ΣX_i=t with t in a pd-ideal J of a base S, giving a cosimplicial pd-dga C_DRpd[n](S,J,t) ≅ S<X_0..X_{n-1}>⊗Λ(dX) resolving S
ideas.modern_name: cosimplicial divided-power de Rham algebra over a pd-base; simplex in a pd-neighbourhood (cf. crystalline site, pd-envelope of the diagonal)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; closest are crystalline-style pd-envelopes (Berthelot) and later cosimplicial pd-algebra models (Ekedahl; Toën's affine stacks; Mondal-Reinecke unipotent homotopy)

ideas.what: Pd Poincaré lemma: S<X_1..X_m>⊗Λ[dX_i] is a resolution of S

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes an integral (pd) analogue of Sullivan's simplicial forms by using a parametrized simplex ΣX_i=t with t a divided-power element of the base. The universal case is the pd-line S=Z<t>. Over Q with t inverted this specializes to Sullivan's forms, so it is an integral pd-lattice in a degenerating family of A_PL's. He notes it only maps to, and does not compute, H^*(X,S). The question of what this cosimplicial pd-dga actually computes (e.g. for S=Z_p, J=(p), t=p, or the universal Z<t>) seems not to have been pursued under this form.
missed.quote: les équations ΣX_i = 1 de E^[n] par l'équation ΣX_i = t dans S^{n+1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic commutative cochain models (Mandell, Toën's schematization, Mondal-Reinecke, Yuan's integral models) are active topics. A 1976 pd-simplex construction with a deformation parameter t, interpolating between a pd/crystalline degenerate fiber at t=0 and Sullivan's forms at t invertible, is a concrete, testable model that might be compared to those approaches.

missed.claim: The page implicitly links Sullivan rational homotopy theory with crystalline (pd) methods: simplices whose vertices are pd-close to each other, i.e. the simplex sits in a pd-neighbourhood of the diagonal. This anticipates using pd/crystalline structures to model integral homotopy types (Ekedahl 2002 and later), apparently without credit to Grothendieck's 1976 IHES talk.
missed.quote: un "paramètre" t ∈ S (i.e. t ∈ J, J idéal à p.d. de S) pouvant prendre des p.d.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and a possibly distinct construction (pd-simplex of size t) relative to the existing integral models.

deep.surprise_reason: A real, unpublished construction: an integral pd-version of Sullivan's forms using a pd-parameter simplex ΣX_i=t. It predates comparable integral pd-models and is not credited to Grothendieck. However, it is a sketch with an acknowledged failure to compute integral cohomology, and the underlying pd Poincaré lemma is standard.
